summary:
I checked each service directly. I fetched its JSON with an Origin header and recorded the CORS header and the field list, then read the terms in the publisher's own metadata (ArcGIS item JSON, the service's iteminfo or metadata XML, or the agency web page). WebFetch could not resolve hosts in this session, so every page was read with curl through the proxy. No number below comes from news or trade sources.

CORS on ArcGIS REST. Esri's ArcGIS Server documentation says: "By default, ArcGIS Server allows cross-domain requests (CORS) so JavaScript clients can invoke the server's services from any domain." The default value of AllowedOrigins is "*". The ArcGIS Online documentation says: "By default, ArcGIS REST API is open to CORS requests from web applications on any domain." and "All currently supported versions of ArcGIS Server support CORS by default." In my tests, 35 distinct ArcGIS hosts answered a GET with Access-Control-Allow-Origin, either * or the origin I sent. Three hosts could not be tested:
- public.gis.lacounty.gov returned 403 from a bot-protection page.
- geodata.md.gov returned 503 for maintenance; the mirror mdgeodata.md.gov worked.
- nhgeodata.unh.edu failed TLS chain verification.
Query limits per request are 1,000–5,000 records (NY: 50,000), so a page should query one parcel at a time, by point or by ID.

(a) Official free statewide parcel REST services I verified (fields checked):

Value, land use, site address and sale price all present: FL, MA, NJ, CT, CO, DC, MN (59 opt-in counties), NE.
- MD has a consideration amount and transfer date.
- NC has a sale date but no price.

Value, land use and address, no sale price: TX, UT (LIR county layers), MT, WA, NY (38 counties including NYC), WI, VT, AR, ID (13 counties), ND (tax-roll table), WY (values and address, no use code).

Geometry or address only: VA, DE, HI, WV (tax year 2023), RI (2019–2022, semi-restricted), OH (use code and address, last updated Jan 2024), IN (class code and address), ME (location only).

TN offers per-county shapefile downloads only. It has no REST service and excludes 9 counties, including Davidson, Shelby and Knox.

No official public statewide service was found for: AL, AK, AZ, CA, GA, IL, IA, KS, KY, LA, MI, MS, MO, NV, NM, OK, PA, SC, SD. OR's statewide taxlot service needs a token. PR's CRIM parcel service reports "not started".

Explicit licenses are rare:
- CT is CC0 and DC is CC BY 4.0.
- WI says "free for public consumption".
- UT says "no constraints".
- AR says "downloaded and utilized in any manner".
- MD allows free distribution with acknowledgement.
- CO forbids resale but allows commercial use with attribution.
- TN allows any use of its downloads.
- NJ and IN request credit.
- Most others carry only disclaimers.

County services:
- Maricopa (sale price and date, full cash value, use code, address).
- Cook (values, class, address, sale date).
- San Diego, through SANDAG (assessed values, land use, address).
- Orange (assessed values, general-plan land use, zoning, address; updated nightly).
- NYC MapPLUTO (land use, assessed values, address).
- Franklin OH (sale price and date, values, use code).
- Fulton (land use code and address only).
- Allegheny and Clark (geometry and ID only).
- Philadelphia OPA through the city's Carto SQL API (market value, sale price and date; CORS *).
- LA County could not be tested (bot wall).
- No Wayne County service was found.

(b) Geocoders:
- Census Geocoder: no CORS. The documentation says so, and my requests got no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header. JSONP works (format=jsonp&callback=..., tested). Batch files take up to 10,000 records but need a POST, so they cannot be called from a browser. Results are interpolated on TIGER address ranges. The pages I read state no rate limit.
- Nominatim: sends CORS *. Its policy caps use at 1 request per second summed over all users of an application, bans client-side autocomplete, requires an identifying Referer or User-Agent and attribution (ODbL), and has an explicit clause on LLM-suggested and vibe-coded use.
- Photon (komoot): sends CORS *. It supports typeahead, asks for fair use, says heavy use is throttled, and gives no availability guarantee.
- Free state locators with CORS and no key: NY and TN (only their own state).
- Esri World Geocoder: answered without a token and with CORS in my test. However, Esri's documentation lists the token as required and prohibits storing results without forStorage=true and a token.

Paid options (Esri, Mapbox, Geoapify, LocationIQ) all put a key that anyone can see into a static page. Each vendor designs for this and offers referrer or origin restrictions. LocationIQ states that referrer restrictions are "a deterrent, not a security boundary".

sources.name: Esri documentation: CORS defaults for ArcGIS Server and ArcGIS Online REST
sources.state_or_scope: All ArcGIS REST services (Enterprise/Server and ArcGIS Online hosted)
sources.fields: n/a
sources.browser_use: yes by default. Esri: 'By default, ArcGIS Server allows cross-domain requests (CORS) so JavaScript clients can invoke the server's services from any domain.' ArcGIS Online (https://doc.arcgis.com/en/arcgis-online/administer/configure-security.htm): 'By default, ArcGIS REST API is open to CORS requests from web applications on any domain.' Empirical check on 2026-11-09: 35 distinct ArcGIS hosts answered a GET carrying an Origin header with Access-Control-Allow-Origin (* or the origin echoed back). 3 hosts could not be tested (LA County: 403 bot wall; geodata.md.gov: 503 maintenance; nhgeodata.unh.edu: TLS chain error).
sources.terms_quote: A property named AllowedOrigins controls this behavior (its default setting is the wildcard symbol *). ... All currently supported versions of ArcGIS Server support CORS by default.
sources.notes: Administrators can narrow AllowedOrigins, so any single service may still refuse; test each endpoint. Esri also warns: 'Settings for CORS headers implemented at the web adaptor, reverse proxy, or load balancer can interfere with ArcGIS Server settings defined by the AllowedOrigins property.' Several state servers echo the origin and add Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true; ArcGIS Online hosts return *.

sources.browser_use: yes: HTTP 200 with Access-Control-Allow-Origin echoing the request origin; maxRecordCount 5000
sources.terms_quote: The State of North Carolina or any employee, representative, or contractor employed by the State assumes no legal responsibility for the content of this information. Data may be accessed and viewed online.
sources.redistribution: unclear: the metadata only disclaims and points to https://www.nconemap.gov/pages/terms, which is rendered by JavaScript and could not be read
sources.notes: Brief PDF (https://it.nc.gov/documents/files/nc-parcels-brief/open): 'All 100 counties participate.' Copyright text: 'NC Center for Geographic Information and Analysis (NCCGIA), NC County Governments, US EPA'. Covers Wake and Mecklenburg.

sources.fields: Land use: DOR_UC, PA_UC. Values: JV (just value), AV_SD/AV_NSD, TV_SD/TV_NSD, LND_VAL. Sales: SALE_PRC1, SALE_YR1, SALE_MO1, QUAL_CD1 and a second sale (…2). Site address: PHY_ADDR1, PHY_CITY, PHY_ZIPCD.
sources.terms_quote: The Department does not generate or maintain the data used to compile this statewide parcel map. The Department does not guarantee the accuracy, or completeness, or the compliance with public records laws of this parcel GIS data.
sources.redistribution: unclear: disclaimer only; credit line given is 'Florida’s county property appraisers, Florida Department of Revenue Property Tax Oversight'
sources.notes: Item description: 'The GIS linework and related attributions for the statewide parcel map are updated annually by the Department every August. Minor data maintenance is also completed every May and November.' Snippet: 'require users to zoom into1:250,000 to view the over 10.8 million parcels'. Covers Miami-Dade.

sources.name: Wisconsin Statewide Parcels V12 (Statewide Parcel Map Initiative)

sources.terms_quote: This data free for public consumption as of: 06/30/2026
sources.redistribution: yes (stated free for public consumption); credit: Wisconsin State Cartographer's Office / WLIP at DOA
sources.notes: The older service name Wisconsin_Statewide_Parcels now returns 'Invalid URL'; use Wisconsin_Statewide_Parcels_DB (layer V1200_WisconsinParcels_2026).

sources.name: MassGIS Massachusetts Property Tax Parcels (Level 3 + assessor extract)
sources.geography: Parcel polygons, stacked where several assessor records share a parcel
sources.frequency_years: not stated in metadata I could read (item modified 2026-10-30)
sources.fields: Land use: USE_CODE, USE_DESC. Values: TOTAL_VAL, LAND_VAL, BLDG_VAL, FY. Sale: LS_PRICE, LS_DATE. Site address: SITE_ADDR, LOCATION, CITY, ZIP.
sources.terms_quote: Assessor’s parcel mapping is a representation of property boundaries, not an authoritative source.
sources.redistribution: unclear: the license field holds only a disclaimer; the mass.gov data page returned 403 to my automated client
sources.notes: The item and the layer disagree on Boston. Item: 'Standardization of assessor parcel mapping is complete for all 351 Massachusetts' cities and towns.' Layer: '(Boston, which is not part of this project, is being processed separately)'.

sources.name: UGRC Utah Statewide Parcels + county LIR (Land Information Records) parcels
sources.geography: Parcel polygons for 29 counties; tax-roll attributes in per-county LIR layers
sources.frequency_years: monthly for the 5 largest counties, quarterly to annually for others; LIR annually
sources.fields: Statewide layer: PARCEL_ADD, PARCEL_CITY, PARCEL_ZIP, OWN_TYPE (no values). LIR layers: PROP_CLASS, PROP_TYPE, TOTAL_MKT_VALUE, LAND_MKT_VALUE, PARCEL_ADD, BUILT_YR. No sale price or date.
sources.terms_quote: There are no constraints or warranties with regard to the use of this dataset. Users are encouraged to attribute content to: State of Utah, SGID.
sources.notes: Same page: 'We aim to update the basic parcels for Davis, Salt Lake, Utah, Washington, and Weber, also known as the Big 5, every month. The rest of the rural counties are on a rotating schedule ranging from quarterly to annually. LIR parcels are updated annually with county year end tax roll information when provided.' The statewide item notes HB113: 'The intent of the bill was to not include any attributes that the counties rely on for data sales.'

sources.name: Montana Cadastral Framework (Montana State Library / Dept. of Revenue ORION)
sources.geography: Parcel polygons, most of the state
sources.fields: Use: PropType plus agricultural acre classes. Values: TotalValue, TotalLandValue, TotalBuildingValue. Property address: AddressLine1, AddressLine2, CityStateZip. No sale price or date.
sources.browser_use: yes: Access-Control-Allow-Origin echoes the origin; maxRecordCount 2000
sources.terms_quote: The Montana State Library provides this product/service for informational purposes only. The Library did not produce it for, nor is it suitable for legal, engineering, or surveying purposes.
sources.redistribution: with restrictions: the same text cites Montana Code Annotated 2-6-1017 on using owner lists as distribution lists; no explicit license
sources.notes: MSL page (https://msl.mt.gov/geoinfo/msdi/cadastral/): 'Cadastral data are provided monthly for each Montana county in file geodatabase and shapefile data formats.'

sources.name: TxGIO StratMap Land Parcels (most recent)
sources.geography: Parcel polygons from appraisal districts; not every county
sources.fields: Land use: stat_land_use, loc_land_use. Values: land_value, imp_value, mkt_value. Site address: situs_addr, situs_city, situs_zip. Also tax_year, date_acq. No sale fields.
sources.browser_use: yes: Access-Control-Allow-Origin echoes the origin; maxRecordCount 2000
sources.terms_quote: TxGIO collects these data to allow end users to acquire statewide land parcel data in one location at no cost.
sources.redistribution: unclear: free of charge, but the FAQ I read gives no license text
sources.notes: FAQ: 'TxGIO will attempt to refresh annually from each appraisal district or their third party vendor.' and 'Not all counties are available for download from TxGIO.' This is the statewide source for Harris, Dallas and Travis where those districts shared data; county availability was not checked.

sources.name: Washington State Current Parcels (WaTech / WA Geoportal)
sources.fields: Land use: LANDUSE_CD (DOR codes), ORIG_LANDUSE_CD. Values: VALUE_LAND, VALUE_BLDG. Site address: SITUS_ADDRESS, SITUS_CITY_NM, SITUS_ZIP_NR. DATA_LINK points to the assessor. No sale fields.
sources.terms_quote: The Washington State Geoportal provides this product/service for informational purposes only.
sources.notes: Description: 'provides a statewide dataset of tax parcels attributes that covers all 39 counties.' Covers King County.

sources.name: Parcels and MOD-IV Composite of NJ, Web Mercator (NJOGIS)
sources.geography: Parcel polygons joined to MOD-IV tax list
sources.frequency_years: not stated in item metadata read
sources.fields: Land use: PROP_CLASS, PROP_USE, BLDG_CLASS. Values: LAND_VAL, IMPRVT_VAL, NET_VALUE. Sale: SALE_PRICE, DEED_DATE, SALES_CODE. Site address: PROP_LOC, plus MUN_NAME and ZIP5.
sources.terms_quote: Acknowledgement of the service provider, NJ Office of Information Technology, Office of GIS (NJOGIS), is requested for maps, data or other products derived from this service.
sources.notes: Snippet: 'The OWNER_NAME field is redacted per Daniel's Law for public web access.'

sources.name: Connecticut CAMA and Parcel Layer (CT GIS Office / OPM)
sources.geography: Parcel polygons for all 169 municipalities with CAMA joined
sources.fields: Land use: State_Use, State_Use_Description, Zone. Values: Assessed_Total, Assessed_Land, Assessed_Building, Appraised_*. Sales: Sale_Price, Sale_Date, Prior_Sale_Price, Prior_Sale_Date. Site address: Location, Property_City, Property_Zip.
sources.terms_quote: licenseInfo: CC0. accessInformation: The State of Connecticut assume no legal responsibility for the information contained herein.
sources.notes: Description: 'each municipality is required to transmit a digital parcel file and an accompanying assessor’s database file (known as a CAMA report), to its respective regional council of governments (COG) by May 1 annually.' and 'geometries for all 169 municipalities and attribution from the CAMA data for all but one municipality.' Some towns suppress owner names. Coordinate system is now EPSG 6434.

sources.name: Maryland Parcel Boundaries (MD iMAP / MDP / SDAT)

sources.frequency_years: not stated (dates carried in SDATDATE, MDPVDATE, POLYDATE fields)

sources.terms_quote: The Data can be freely distributed as long as the metadata entry is not modified or deleted. Any data derived from the Data must acknowledge the State of Maryland in the metadata.
sources.redistribution: yes, with acknowledgement of the State of Maryland
sources.notes: Layer description: 'This dataset contains parcel polygons of the entire state attributed with data from the State Department of Assessments and Taxation and Maryland Department of Planning.'

sources.name: US Census Geocoder (Geocoding Services API)
sources.geography: Address to interpolated point on TIGER address ranges (optionally census geographies)
sources.fields: coordinates x/y, matchedAddress, addressComponents, tigerLine side and ID
sources.browser_use: JSONP only, no CORS. My GET with an Origin header returned no Access-Control-Allow-Origin (only 'Vary: Origin'), and an OPTIONS preflight returned none. format=jsonp&callback=cb returned '/**/cb({...})'.
sources.terms_quote: At this time the geocoder does not support CORS requests so the callback and format parameters should be used in the client to make calls to the geocoder.
sources.redistribution: unclear: no terms or rate limits stated on the pages read
sources.notes: API doc: 'There is currently an upper limit of 10,000 records per batch file.' Batch is a multipart POST, so it cannot be used from a browser without CORS. Census documentation page (https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/geography/technical-documentation/complete-technical-documentation/census-geocoder.html): 'Coordinate results are interpolated, or approximated, based on the physical location that the address geocoded on the TIGER address ranges.' Batch accepts PR addresses with Urbanization. No key needed.

sources.name: OpenStreetMap Nominatim (nominatim.openstreetmap.org)
sources.fields: lat, lon, display_name, address (with addressdetails)
sources.browser_use: technically yes: access-control-allow-origin: * (tested), but bound by the usage policy
sources.terms_quote: No heavy uses (an absolute maximum of 1 request per second). Provide a valid HTTP Referer or User-Agent identifying the application (stock User-Agents as set by http libraries will not do).
sources.redistribution: with attribution; 'Data is provided under the ODbL license which requires to share alike'
sources.notes: Limits are per application: 'the usage limits above apply per website/application : the sum of traffic by all your users should not exceed the limits.' Autocomplete is banned: 'Auto-complete search This is not yet supported by Nominatim and you must not implement such a service on the client side using the API.' LLM clause: 'The public Nominatim API must not be built into, offered through, suggested by, or automatically generated by no-code, low-code, or vibe-coding platforms as a generic geocoding, address lookup, place search, or map search service.' Apps 'must make sure that they can switch the service at our request at any time'.

sources.name: Photon (komoot public instance)
sources.frequency_years: n/a ('Minutely up to date OSM data')
sources.fields: GeoJSON features with name, street, housenumber, city, postcode, coordinates
sources.terms_quote: You can use the API for your project, but please be fair - extensive usage will be throttled. We do not guarantee for the availability and usage might be subject of change in the future.
sources.redistribution: OSM-derived ('Made with OpenStreetMap'); attribution expected; no other license text on the page
sources.notes: Unlike Nominatim, the home page advertises 'Typeahead suggestion', so autocomplete is an intended use. Gives no availability guarantee and no stated numeric limit.

sources.name: State ArcGIS locators with no key: NYS ITS Street_and_Address_Composite; TNMap TN_COMPOSITE
sources.geography: Address to point (address points, then street-segment interpolation)
sources.fields: address, location (NY returns EPSG:26918 unless outSR=4326 is passed; TN returns 4326), score
sources.browser_use: yes: both returned results without a token and with Access-Control-Allow-Origin echoing the origin
sources.terms_quote: The SAM Address Points are the most accurate data available and should be picked anytime a result is returned from one of the SAM address point locators.
sources.redistribution: unclear: no usage terms or limits found on the pages read
sources.notes: Other states may run similar public locators; only NY and TN were tested.

sources.name: Esri ArcGIS World Geocoding Service (paid; API key)
sources.fields: candidates[].address, location, score
sources.browser_use: CORS yes (origin echoed). In my test an anonymous call without a token returned a result, but the documentation lists token as required.
sources.terms_quote: Applications are contractually prohibited from storing the results of geocoding transactions unless they make the request by passing the forStorage parameter with a value of true and the token parameter with a valid token.
sources.redistribution: no storage without forStorage=true and a token (paid)
sources.notes: Key exposure (https://developers.arcgis.com/documentation/security-and-authentication/api-key-authentication/): 'An API key is a long-lived access token created using API key credentials. They are valid for up to one year and are typically embedded directly into client applications.' and 'It is also recommended that you set referrer URLs in order to enhance the security of the token.' A key in a static page is therefore visible to anyone; referrer restriction is the mitigation.

sources.name: Mapbox Geocoding (public pk token)
sources.fields: n/a (endpoint not tested; needs a token)
sources.browser_use: designed for browsers with a public token; not tested here
sources.terms_quote: Public tokens are designed to be used in client-side applications, meaning they can be safely exposed in web browsers, mobile apps, and other client environments.
sources.notes: Same doc: 'When you add a URL restriction to a token, that token will only work for requests that originate from the URLs you specify. Tokens without restrictions will work for requests originating from any URL.' and 'private tokens should never be exposed in client-side code.'

sources.name: Geoapify Geocoding / Address Autocomplete (API key)
sources.fields: n/a (not tested; needs a key)
sources.browser_use: key sits in page source; restrict by origin (not tested here)
sources.terms_quote: Optionally, you can protect the API key by listing allowed IP addresses, HTTP referrers, origins, and CORS.
sources.notes: How-to page (https://apidocs.geoapify.com/how-to/addresses/address-to-coordinates/): 'In browser applications, restrict the API key to the application’s allowed origins.'

sources.name: LocationIQ (pk. API token)
sources.fields: n/a (not tested; needs a token)
sources.browser_use: public pk. tokens are intended for websites; restrictions only deter misuse (not tested here)
sources.terms_quote: The referrer is an HTTP header that is sent by browsers and like all HTTP headers, it can be spoofed. Treat referrer restrictions as a deterrent, not a security boundary, and pair them with scoped access tokens and frequent access token rotation.
sources.notes: Same page: 'You can use access tokens in both public (websites, apps) and private environments (server backends).' Per-token per-IP, per-second and daily caps can be set. 'Do not use IP restrictions for browser-based use-cases such as showing Maps or an Autocomplete widget.'

open_questions: No official, public, free statewide parcel REST service was found for AL, AK, AZ, CA, GA, IL, IA, KS, KY, LA, MI, MS, MO, NV, NM, OK, SC, SD. The checks were ArcGIS Online catalog searches plus web searches, and absence was not proven. Only private or academic copies turned up, e.g. 'Iowa Statewide Parcel Data, 2017' (Univ. of Iowa) and 'Parcels_MS Statewide 2022' (an engineering firm). These were not treated as official.

Pennsylvania: PASDA's https://apps.pasda.psu.edu/arcgis/rest/services/PA_Parcels/MapServer/1 is a compiled parcel layer with fields PIN, Source and Date only. It sends CORS, but no license or description text was found, so it is not listed as a source.

Oregon: the ODF statewide taxlot service (https://gis.odf.oregon.gov/ags1/rest/services/WebMercator/StatewideTaxLots/MapServer) returned 'Token Required'. No public statewide Oregon taxlot service was verified.

Puerto Rico: the CRIM parcel service https://sigejp.pr.gov/server/rest/services/crim/crim_parcelas/MapServer returned 'Service crim/crim_parcelas/MapServer not started' (HTTP 500 in JSON) on 2026-11-09. Retry later and check its terms.
Wayne County, MI: no official county parcel service was found. Neither a Wayne County nor a City of Detroit parcel layer was verified.
LA County: public.gis.lacounty.gov answered my script with an Incapsula bot-protection 403, so fields, CORS and current terms need a check from a real browser. The ArcGIS item is from 2020.

Harris, Dallas and Travis (TX) county-specific services were not checked; they rely on StratMap if the district shared data. Miami-Dade (FL), King (WA), Hennepin (MN), Wake and Mecklenburg (NC) are covered by the verified statewide layers, but their county-specific services were not checked.

Several items have only disclaimers and no license, so whether derived numbers may be shown publicly is unclear: NC, FL, MA, TX, WA, VT, VA, WV, DE, HI, ME, NH, ND, WY, MN, NE and all county services. Ask the publishers before showing values. Nebraska's text says 'for official, internal use'. Rhode Island requires a disclaimer in any public viewer.

Pages I could not read: mass.gov (HTTP 403 to automated client; holds MassGIS update frequency and terms), www.nconemap.gov/pages/terms (JavaScript-only), and the Minnesota Geospatial Commons license page (JavaScript-only hub). nhgeodata.unh.edu failed TLS chain verification, so its fields and CORS are unverified.
Census Geocoder: no request-rate limit or terms-of-use text was found on the API page or the Census documentation page. The only documented limit is 10,000 records per batch file.
Mapbox, Geoapify and LocationIQ geocoding endpoints were not called (they need keys), so their CORS headers were not observed. Only their documentation on exposing keys was read.
Esri World Geocoder answered an anonymous findAddressCandidates call with CORS, contradicting the documentation's 'token ... required'. Do not rely on anonymous access.
Update frequency is not stated for NJ, MD, WA (only 'Updated April 2026'), HI, ME, NH, OH (last update Jan 21, 2024), VA, DE and most county services.

Tool note: the WebFetch tool failed DNS for every host in this session, so all pages and services were read with curl through the session proxy (CA bundle at /root/.ccr/ca-bundle.crt).
